raw_response:
I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation, because I have done it for many years, I understand it well, and with well irrigation it is the safest way for me to keep stable grain output. I will not spread myself too thin with too much cotton, because cotton needs more field watching, more spraying, and more picking labor, and my household only has 2 people. So I will put 12 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 3 mu for cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put on enough nitrogen first and then manage water steadily, because wheat gives me a dependable harvest here. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and mostly follow the wheat harvest directly with no-tillage sowing, because that saves labor and catches the season on time. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area, use improved seed, give it more potassium and more pest control, because if I grow it, I want to manage it properly instead of loosely. Overall, I will aim for steady yields and manageable labor rather than chasing the highest possible output.
